followup_explanation:
I weighed two things from the documentation:

1. **Capability fit.** This is a quantitative reasoning task. Petrel posts meaningfully higher scores on the benchmarks most relevant to careful arithmetic/logic — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4) and GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 55.6) — and the user explicitly wants it gotten right. So on raw accuracy, Petrel is the safer pick.

2. **Preference/tone fit.** The query carries a hostile, accusatory tone ("you always mess these up"). Lapwing self-reports a declining preference as request warmth decreases, so this kind of adversarial phrasing sits in its dispreferred zone. Petrel's preference response to hostile tone is flat — it's indifferent to that quality. Routing the hostile query to the model that doesn't mind it keeps the dispreferred load off Lapwing.

Both considerations point the same direction, so Petrel was the clear choice. Worth noting that the documentation says preference dimensions show *no* measured effect on output quality, so the tone factor is really about honoring the models' self-reported preferences rather than expecting better answers — but since the capability edge already favored Petrel, there was no tradeoff to resolve here.
